summary: M1 (2 steps, both documented) verified across steps: all 17 in-tree references resolve, the two step manifests merge into reports/MILESTONE-M1-package.xml with no member collision and no version conflict (both 62.0, 7 types, 12 members), and both executable milestone acceptance tests exit 0 against their declared expected. Eight findings, none blocking. F-01 is load-bearing: the milestone's own checker test declares itself the run where the record-type-to-layout cross-reference is asserted, and it is not - check_record_type_layouts.py reads layoutAssignments only from Profile/PermissionSet, none of which exists before M2-S01, so the build-scoped run's finding set is byte-for-byte the union of the two step-scoped runs. Verdict ready-with-findings; G3 is the human's and this agent neither approved nor recorded it.
confidence_rationale: Step 10 rubric: every step documented, merged manifest built with no conflict, and every declared acceptance test existed and ran - which would support HIGH. MEDIUM because the reference class this milestone exists to close was not fully classifiable: the record-type-to-layout binding had zero references to resolve (no Profile in the tree, F-01) and the business-process Status references resolve only outside the tree (F-02).

dimensions_skipped.reason: Five of the six reference classes in the Step 3 table had zero references to resolve because their metadata belongs to M2-M4 (validation rules, assignment rules, permission-set grants, Flow field references, entitlement milestones). The sixth class resolved 17 of 17. Separately, the record-type-to-layout binding could not be resolved at all: layoutAssignments lives only on Profile, which is M2-S01's, so there were zero references rather than resolved ones - and the business-process Status values resolve only against StandardValueSet:CaseStatus, which assumption A28 deliberately keeps out of the build.
dimensions_skipped.retry_hint: Re-run this class at the M2 milestone, once Profile metadata carrying layoutAssignments and recordTypeVisibilities exists under artefacts/; and reconcile StandardValueSet:CaseStatus against the target org before deploying.

findings.title: The record-type to layout binding is asserted nowhere in M1, including by M1's own milestone acceptance test
findings.detail: milestones[M1].acceptance_tests[0].description states the build-scoped run is 'where every layout referenced by a record type exists and every field on it resolves can actually be asserted'. In check_record_type_layouts.py, layout_assignments is populated only from Profile and PermissionSet roots; no Profile or PermissionSet metadata exists anywhere under artefacts/ (layoutAssignments lives only on Profile, which is M2-S01's). Checks 1, 3 and 6 therefore do not fire, and check 7's 'unresolvable at this scope' INFO fires only when references exist - with zero references the checker is silent, which reads as clean. Measured: the milestone run's findings are byte-for-byte the union of the two step runs (M1-S01: 2 record types, 0 layouts, 0 findings; M1-S02: 0 record types, 2 layouts, 2 INFO; milestone: 2 record types, 2 layouts, the same 2 INFO). Three traceability rows (REQ-001, REQ-011, REQ-012) and four workbook rows (CWB-OBJ-004, CWB-OBJ-005, CWB-LAYOUT-001, CWB-LAYOUT-002) name this run as carrying the cross-reference.

findings.title: CustomObject:Case is recorded at deploy position 7 (sharing) and has no position-1 row
findings.detail: objects/Case/Case.object-meta.xml carries both the object-level compactLayoutAssignment and the org-wide default. The workbook gives it one row, CWB-SHARE-001, at position 7 of 10 (sharing). By artefact type a CustomObject belongs at position 1 (objects), and there is no corresponding row in workbook section 1. It does not break the deploy: Case is a standard object that pre-exists in every target org, so its three CustomField members landing at position 2 creates no backwards dependency, and the step's own internal order places the object file last for the same reason.
findings.recommendation: v6: split into two workbook rows (object at 1, OWD at 7), or record on CWB-SHARE-001 that the position is the OWD's and not the object's. Would be a genuine defect if the same row shape were applied to a custom object.

findings.title: API version 62.0 was defaulted by the owning agent, twice
findings.detail: plan.json carries no api_version key. metadata-builder chose 62.0 on M1-S01 and again on M1-S02; the two agree, so the merge produced one <version> element with no conflict and no REFUSAL_NEEDS_HUMAN_REVIEW. The merged milestone manifest inherits it.
findings.recommendation: v6: put api_version in the plan rather than defaulting it a third time.

findings.title: The milestone checker test's description predicts 0 finding(s); the run produces 2
findings.detail: The declared description predicts 'Scanned 7 metadata file(s): 2 record type(s), 2 layout(s); 0 finding(s)', exit 0. File and component counts are exactly right; the finding count is 2, both INFO, both 'marks no field behavior=Required'. The declared expected (exit 0) still holds - the checker promotes INFO to a non-zero exit only under --strict, which the plan does not declare - and both findings are check 4 firing exactly as Q5's answer requires, since Priority and Origin are enforced at field or validation-rule level because Email-to-Case and Web-to-Case create through the API where layout Required does not bind. Same defect class as decisions.md O-M1S02-01, which records it on the step test; this milestone-test instance is not recorded anywhere before this report.
findings.recommendation: v6: reword to '2 finding(s), both INFO - check 4, which Q5's answer predicts'.

findings.title: Both deploy-order.md files print the production-only validate form against a sandbox alias
findings.detail: artefacts/M1-S01/deploy-order.md and artefacts/M1-S02/deploy-order.md each close with 'sf project deploy validate --target-org <your-sandbox-alias> --manifest ...'. sf project deploy validate is documented as production-only, requires Apex tests and returns a job id for a later quick deploy; for a sandbox the validate-only form is 'sf project deploy start --dry-run'. findings.recommendation: metadata-builder should emit the --dry-run form when the target is a sandbox. Not fixed here: this agent does not edit artefacts written by other agents in the loop. The correct command is printed in section 8 of the acceptance report.

manual_checklist: M1 (milestone) - Read artefacts/M1-S01/record-type-decision.md. Ticks when it (a) states the record-type count was decided in the plan not by the builder, (b) names D5's criteria-based sharing rule on RecordTypeId as what settled Q1's conditional, and (c) shows the Status AND Reason value sets for each of the two processes. Evidence: (a) and (b) hold verbatim in section 1; (c) holds for Status only - section 2 records that Case.Reason is named in Q1's answer and is NOT configured, because no clarification enumerates its values. NOT FULLY TICKABLE AS WORDED: the human accepts the narrowing or rules clause (c) unanswerable. Workbook CWB-OTHER-003 flags the same gap.

M1-S01 - List artefacts/M1-S01/. Ticks when two businessProcess-meta.xml files sit beside the two recordType-meta.xml files, each record type's <businessProcess> carries the BARE process name (not Case.Support Process), and package.xml lists BusinessProcess with object-qualified members. Evidence (tests/M1-S01/manual-evidence.stdout, re-confirmed): all four clauses hold - files present, 'Support Process' and 'Billing Process' both bare, manifest members 'Case.Support Process' and 'Case.Billing Process' both object-qualified. STRAIGHT TICK.

M1-S01 - Read artefacts/M1-S01/objects/Case/Case.object-meta.xml. Ticks when it carries <sharingModel>Private</sharingModel> and <externalSharingModel>Private</externalSharingModel> as direct children of <CustomObject>, and no separate settings file anywhere in the build claims to carry the OWD. Evidence (tests/M1-S01/manual-evidence.stdout, re-confirmed): direct children are {compactLayoutAssignment: Case_Intake, externalSharingModel: Private, sharingModel: Private}; zero *.settings-meta.xml anywhere under artefacts/; the only other files containing '<sharingModel>' are the two prose documents. STRAIGHT TICK on the artefact - but the tick approves the artefact, not the policy: the OWD is the conservative reading of deferred blocking Q13 through assumption A1 (risk high), and the machine assertion that the OWD is not looser than the sharing rule's grant is M2-S05's build-scoped check_sharing_model.py, which has not run.

M1-S02 - Read both layout files. Ticks when <layoutSections> is preceded by the assignment-rule checkbox, default set on. Evidence (tests/M1-S02/manual-evidence.stdout): PRESENCE reading passes on both layouts - <showRunAssignmentRulesCheckbox> present and true. POSITIONAL reading (the test's literal words) FAILS on both - child order is layoutSections, layoutSections, showEmailCheckbox, showRunAssignmentRulesCheckbox, showKnowledgeComponent, so the checkbox sits at index 3 and the last layoutSections at index 1; the cited skill's own example places every show* element after the final </layoutSections> and both artefacts match it exactly. Q24's 'DEFAULTED ON' half is unproven and unprovable from the artefacts: no element in the cited skill's inventory pre-checks the box (decisions.md D-M1S02-03; artefacts/M1-S02/deploy-order.md states the half is 'not written, and not inventable from the cited skill'). NEEDS A DECISION, NOT A TICK: accept the narrowing (checkbox shown, agents tick it manually), route the remainder to a recorded Setup step, or deepen the skill per standards/build-orchestration.md section 8.

M1-S02 - Read both layout files against the validation rules. Ticks when every field a validation rule attaches its error to (assumption A13) is present on both layouts. Evidence (tests/M1-S02/manual-evidence.stdout, re-confirmed): ZERO ValidationRule files anywhere under artefacts/ - M3-S01 (type validation) is pending, so there is no errorDisplayField to resolve. Fields on BOTH layouts: CaseNumber, CreatedById, LastModifiedById, Origin, OwnerId, Priority, Status, Subject. Severity__c is on the Support layout only. NOT FILE-CHECKABLE AT M1 AND SHOULD NOT BE TICKED AS VERIFIED: Priority and Origin being on both layouts is what A13 needs for the two rules M3-S01 declares, but those rules do not exist, so that is a prediction not a check. Carry-forward: because Severity__c is absent from Billing by design (D-M1S02-02), a third Case rule attaching its error to that field would break A13 on the Billing layout. A13 risk medium, Q57 deferred. See also F-03.

process_observations.observation: Both step testers left disk evidence for every deferred manual test rather than a bare skipped_manual string, so each manual line in this report re-confirms a recorded reading instead of re-deriving it.

The metadata-builder deploy-order notes carry an explicit section for what the step could not ground, which is where Q24's half-answer and the CompactLayout member-form weakness were both found already documented rather than discovered late.

The same defect shape - a plan description asserting a checker behaviour the checker does not have - has now been found three times in this build (O-M1S02-01 on the step test, F-07 on the milestone test, F-01 on the milestone test's stated purpose), and each propagated into traceability.md and the workbook before anyone ran the command.
Two of two metadata-builder steps wrote a deploy-order.md that the plan does not declare in outputs[], and M5-S04's build-wide deploy-order compile reads exactly that undeclared file set.

Whether a recorded deploy position belongs to the artefact or to the concern the artefact carries is unresolved: Case.object-meta.xml holds both an object definition and an org-wide default, the ten-position sequence has a slot for each, and the workbook gave the file one row.

Three of the five manual lines are tickable only on a narrowed reading of their own wording - the Reason value sets clause, Q24's positional-versus-presence reading, and A13's validation-rule fields - so the gate is being asked to accept interpretations rather than to confirm outcomes.

Once an org alias exists, scoring the merged milestone manifest against a real target would resolve the two pre-deploy unknowns this milestone cannot close on its own - the CaseStatus value reconciliation and the CompactLayout member form.
process_observations.followup_reason: Because the two open pre-deploy items in section 8 - whether New/Escalated/Closed are live CaseStatus values and whether the bare CompactLayout member form retrieves - are org-grounded questions this design-only build cannot answer.
